title: S&P Global Investment Manager Index (Oct 2026) — 10:00 ET, the edition that scores the September lane's date rule out of sample
source: EST: DERIVED BY RULE, NOT READ OFF A CALENDAR — and the derivation is the point. S&P Global's public PMI calendar (pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes, fetched direct 2026-09-09) rolls only ~4 weeks forward: it ends at October 07 and lists the IMI exactly once, on September 15. Its stated 'standard monthly release schedules' block names rules for the Manufacturing, Services and Whole Economy PMIs and NO rule for the IMI. So the October date cannot be read; it can only be derived. Three IMI press releases fetched direct as PDFs this session give masthead release dates 2026-01-13, 2026-05-12 and 2026-08-11 — each the Tuesday eight days after that month's first Monday (2026-01-05, 2026-05-04, 2026-08-03). The same rule reproduces the listed 2026-09-15 exactly from a 2026-09-07 first Monday, so it is 4 for 4 including one forward prediction. October 2026's first Monday is 2026-10-05, giving 2026-10-13. Time-of-day carried from the three primaries, all of which read '1000 EDT/EST'. Filed estimate on two counts and would stay estimate even if listed: the date is a rule output rather than a publisher statement, and market-events-data.ts has no confirmed-source prefix for a private survey compiler. Proposed by the never-assessed initial research of sp-global-investment-manager-index-2026-09-15, 2026-09-09.
notes: PROPOSED SO THE RULE CAN BE WRONG IN PUBLIC. The September ledger's date leg rests on a rule that has never been used forward, and a rule tested only on the dates that built it is not tested at all. This entry is the falsifier with a date on it: when S&P Global's calendar rolls far enough to list October (roughly mid-September), the listing either reads October 13 or it does not, and the September ledger's leg 1 is scored either way. Two structural notes that carry from the parent. It is a MID-MONTH edition on the second Tuesday, unlike September's third — the ordinal moves, the rule does not. And its field window would fall in the week of 2026-10-05, which under this calendar contains ISM Services and the S&P Global Services PMI (both 10-05), the OPEC+ meeting (10-04) and the September jobs report (10-02); September CPI does not land until 2026-10-14, the day AFTER this release — so an October panel would be post-jobs and pre-CPI, the mirror of the September edition's position. And the 10:00 ET slot would NOT be clean the way 2026-09-15's is: existing-home-sales-2026-10-13 already holds that slot on this date, so the September edition keeps its status as the one attribution-clean IMI window in this calendar. NOT A TRADE: symbols is empty, no macro-keyed house playbook, status is estimate, and the parent ledger's call on the September edition is stand-aside on a measured-to-nil 10:00 window.
